title: Adding a usage event touches the event class, docs table, and parse tests together
answers: how do I add a new telemetry event
what files must change when a usage event is added
new event missing from usage tracking docs
where do end-to-end events for log_model and register_model live
body:
A new usage event changes several places together:
- An Event subclass in mlflow/telemetry/events.py with name and a parse() that returns only bounded params. Its comment should say what it covers versus the sub-step event (for example, LogModelEvent vs CreateLoggedModelEvent).
- A top-level public function is wrapped with @record_usage_event(EventClass) from mlflow/telemetry/track.py. Sub-steps that need their own event call _record_event directly (see env_pack).
- A row in docs/docs/community/usage-tracking.mdx with the event's params example.
- Parse parametrized tests and name assertions in tests/telemetry/test_events.py, plus an end-to-end check in tests/telemetry/test_tracked_events.py.
Import events lazily inside functions in model and env modules. events.py imports env_pack lazily to avoid the cycle events -> env_pack -> models.model -> events.
applies: Adding or renaming any usage event in mlflow/telemetry and the modules that emit it.
says: Add telemetry instrumentation to track how often users save or register models.
The public privacy documentation is missing newly tracked product telemetry metrics.
Track usage analytics for model logging operations to understand feature adoption.
Document collected telemetry parameters in the community privacy and usage tracking guide.
search: Adding or renaming a usage tracking event requires updating an Event subclass with bounded parse() params in mlflow/telemetry/events.py, decorating top-level functions with @record_usage_event, adding a documentation row in docs/docs/community/usage-tracking.mdx, and adding tests. Sub-steps call _record_event directly, while tests in tests/telemetry/test_events.py and test_tracked_events.py cover parameter parsing and end-to-end tracking. Events must be imported lazily inside functions in model and env modules, and events.py imports env_pack lazily to prevent circular imports.
